notes.text: Jared McCann is out 10 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 36% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, up from 2% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 53:03 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Kiefer Sherwood is out week to week (upper body injury) and missed their last game.
Alexander Wennberg returned in their last game after missing 2 games.

stakes: The Kraken go in tied for fifth in the Pacific with 21 points, a point behind the Sharks, fourth. A regulation win for the Kraken would lift them past the Sharks. The Kraken have five games in hand.

story.head: Celebrini’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kraken (10-8-1) beat Vancouver 5-1 on Thursday, while the Sharks (10-12-2) lost 5-2 to Calgary on Tuesday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Kraken fifth (tied for 23rd in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth (tied for 20th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Kraken’s record (.553) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.430), largely thanks to their finishing. So is the Sharks’ (.458 on chances worth .399), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Kraken rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd), give up a lot of shots (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (31st). As for the Sharks, they do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). They also are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd), so the Sharks hit a lot, but the Kraken mostly don’t. Both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Berkly Catton (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 19 GP) leads the Kraken in scoring, and Brandon Montour (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 18 GP) is next in line. For the Sharks, Macklin Celebrini (9 G / 18 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in seven straight games against Seattle. Will Smith (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind.
Joey Daccord (4-4-0 / .872 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Seattle, and Alex Nedeljkovic (4-3-1 / .901 SV% in 8 GS) for San Jose.
